result.title: Anytime-Valid Empirical Likelihood Inference from LLM Annotations with Adaptive Human Auditing
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate unlabeled data as a fast, low-cost alternative to human annotation. However, their outputs can be biased and miscalibrated relative to human labels, potentially leading to misleading analysis and inference. We propose AAELI (Adaptive Human Auditing and Anytime-Valid Empirical Likelihood Inference), an online framework for estimating the population mean of human labels under a limited auditing budget. AAELI uses LLM outputs to guide adaptive human auditing and combines them with audited labels through predictable empirical-likelihood $e$-processes to construct anytime-valid confidence sequences. Our main theoretical result shows that a predictably learned efficient projection preserves the first-order profile empirical-likelihood statistic under adaptive auditing, without requiring a prescribed convergence rate for the projection estimator. This yields an exactly anytime-valid betting construction whose continuous-mixture form incurs a scalar rather than vector-dimensional mixing penalty. Supporting results establish adaptive empirical-likelihood asymptotics and show that a learned audit rule attains the oracle variance within the stated class of augmented estimating-equation designs under the same audit-probability floor and long-run expected budget. Experiments on synthetic data and three real-world datasets demonstrate that AAELI maintains empirical anytime coverage while requiring fewer human audits than the strongest competing baseline to reach a target precision.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AAELI 在线框架：用 LLM 标注引导有限预算下的人工抽检，并通过可预测经验似然 e-process 构造 anytime-valid 置信序列，估计人类标签总体均值，理论上证明学习式投影在自适应抽检下保持一阶 profile 统计量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其"用廉价代理信号决定何处花费人工核查预算、并以 anytime-valid 序列支持随时停止"的形式，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的证据获取分配与停止判据提供统计工具线索，但需核查其假设与本任务结构是否相容。
